answer: That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the hollow embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator burns authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Since the vault index is rebuilt each epoch, the quartz audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 75% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That is 27 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
